period_order_check.comparison: period2-to-period3 cyanidin change: mild->hot versus mild->spring return

mechanistic_interpretation: In Moricandia, greater thermal severity under the same stated summer photoperiod strongly depresses floral anthocyanin, and returning plants toward spring conditions restores anthocyanin. Together with summer-white downregulation of MYB90, CHS, U75C1/U78D2 and TTG1, this creates a direct within-species bridge from thermal environment to the pigment network and achromatic phenotype.
hard_nonclaims: post-publication and post-preflight, not an untouched confirmatory test
does not rescue the failed cross-cohort FCP BIO5 replication
the mild-to-hot subset is sequential and can retain period/order carryover, although the reversal sequence argues strongly against a generic third-period decline
does not prove all natural white-flower systems are thermally plastic
does not establish a universal positive temperature effect across species
